sections.text: Total Copper in Acid ( Iodometric Method )

This document outlines the testing 
 procedure P1, which must be performed 
 on a monthly basis
 as indicated by M1 in the above title 
 block

This method can be used for the determination, by 
 titration, of total copper in hydrochloric acid ( HCL) that does not contain a 
 copper complexor. In steel systems, very little copper in solution would be 
 expected.

The copper in the sample 
 is oxidized. Iodine is liberated by reaction of the copper with potassium 
 iodide ( KI ) in proportion to the amount of copper present, and the free 
 iodine is titrated with standard sodium thiosulfate ( Na2S2O3 
 ) solution in the presence of a starch indicator.

items:
The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D

Acids

Keep these 
 acids closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do not 
 breathe them, use only in a hood.

sections.text:
Glasses ( 
Pipettes, Volumetric Flasks, filter paper).

Pipet an aliquot of the filtered sample into an 
 Erlenmeyer flask containing 25 to 50 mL of water. The aliquot should contain 
 enough copper to give a thiosulfate titration of over 5 mL.

Add 5 g of
 KI, stopper the flask, and swirl to dissolve, allow to stand for about 5 min. 
 the liberated iodine will turn the solution yellow to brown in color.

Unstopper the flask and titrate with 0.1 N
 Na2S2O3 solution until most of the 
 reddish-brown color disappear.
Do not titrate to light yellow color.

Add several drops of starch indicator solution 
 and continue the titration until the purple starch-iodine color in the 
 solution disappears.

Record the milliliters of Na2S2O3 
 solution used.

text:
Title
Total Copper in Acid ( Iodometric Method )
Introduction
This document outlines the testing 
 procedure P1, which must be performed 
 on a monthly basis
 as indicated by M1 in the above title 
 block
This method can be used for the determination, by 
 titration, of total copper in hydrochloric acid ( HCL) that does not contain a 
 copper complexor. In steel systems, very little copper in solution would be 
 expected.
Summary of Method
The copper in the sample 
 is oxidized. Iodine is liberated by reaction of the copper with potassium 
 iodide ( KI ) in proportion to the amount of copper present, and the free 
 iodine is titrated with standard sodium thiosulfate ( Na2S2O3 
 ) solution in the presence of a starch indicator.
Safety Precautions
The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D 
 3370-76.
Acids 
 such as hydrochloric acid and others are dangerous, so you have to wear breathing mask.
Keep these 
 acids closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do not 
 breathe them, use only in a hood.
Tools and Equipment
Apparatus
Glasses ( 
Pipettes, Volumetric Flasks, filter paper).
Electronic balance.
Fuming cub ( hood ).
Reagents
Sodium Thiosulfate, Standard Solution ( 0.1N ).
Potassium Iodide ( KI ), granular.
Starch Indicator Solutions.
Work to be Carried Out
Pipet an aliquot of the filtered sample into an 
 Erlenmeyer flask containing 25 to 50 mL of water. The aliquot should contain 
 enough copper to give a thiosulfate titration of over 5 mL.
Add 5 g of
 KI, stopper the flask, and swirl to dissolve, allow to stand for about 5 min. 
 the liberated iodine will turn the solution yellow to brown in color.
Unstopper the flask and titrate with 0.1 N
 Na2S2O3 solution until most of the 
 reddish-brown color disappear.
Do not titrate to light yellow color.
Add several drops of starch indicator solution 
 and continue the titration until the purple starch-iodine color in the 
 solution disappears.
Record the milliliters of Na2S2O3 
 solution used.

Do not titrate to light yellow color.

Record the milliliters of Na2S2O3

Calculation
Copper, % = ( AN / BS )

solution,

titrated, and
